item.text: {"text":"Temporal attention offers a plausible structural change while preserving BERT4Rec. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) combines positional information with learned pairwise time-interval representations; its attention mechanism is useful inspiration, without adopting its causal backbone. More recent work explores adaptive temporal structure: [TiSRec, RecSys 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3759327) learns time-interval-based local preference blocks with intra/inter-block encoders; [Temporal-Series-Aware Adaptive Positional Encoding, WWW 2026](https://doi.org/10.1145/3774904.3792333) incorporates consecutive interaction intervals into adaptive positional features. These motivate learning how temporal spacing affects relevance, but do not establish that recent purchases indicate unresolved demand or guarantee gains on the four Amazon categories.\n\nSuggested experiment, inferred from these mechanisms: retain one bidirectional BERT4Rec per category and add jointly learned per-head relative-position and logarithmically bucketed time-gap biases to attention logits. Scalar biases avoid materializing pairwise hidden-dimensional temporal embeddings, although attention remains quadratic. Let heads learn different temporal sensitivities rather than impose universal recency decay. Keep sampling unchanged to isolate temporal attention. Preserve strict-prefix terminal masked supervision: target item and subsequent events absent; append the reserved MASK and read its final nonpadding position. Use only observed history timestamps; give MASK temporal relations a dedicated unknown bucket, never the held-out target timestamp. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) establishes masked-item training to prevent bidirectional target leakage. Compare position-only, time-only and combined biases under the fixed macro validation HR@10 evaluator; these are proposed ablations, not measured improvements."}
